metadata.summary: Share of people aged 15 and older who can read and write a short statement about everyday life. UNESCO gathers literacy surveys and censuses, and Our World in Data republishes the rate.

metadata.description: Gross adjusted disposable income per capita, PPP converted
metadata.summary: Household income left after taxes and transfers, plus the value of public services, per person in comparable US dollars. The OECD calculates it from each country's national accounts.

Carbon dioxide released each year from fossil fuels and industry, divided by population. The Global Carbon Project assembles national energy and cement statistics, and Our World in Data republishes them.

Average number of days per year, over the five most recent full years, when the temperature falls to 0 degrees Celsius or below. Counts use the daily minimum temperature from the Open-Meteo historical archive, which republishes ECMWF ERA5 under the CC BY 4.0 license.

Average number of days per year, over the five most recent full years, when the temperature reaches at least 30 degrees Celsius. Counts use the daily maximum temperature from the Open-Meteo historical archive, which republishes ECMWF ERA5 under the CC BY 4.0 license.

Average number of days per year, over the five most recent full years, when wind gusts reach at least 60 kilometres per hour. Counts use the daily maximum gust from the Open-Meteo historical archive, which republishes ECMWF ERA5 under the CC BY 4.0 license.

Fixed subscriptions that deliver broadband internet to homes and businesses, counted per 100 people. Telecom operators report the lines to the International Telecommunication Union, which the World Bank republishes.

Gross domestic product per person, converted to current international dollars so prices are comparable across countries. The World Bank compiles it from national accounts in the World Development Indicators.
All government spending on education, from primary school through higher education, as a share of gross domestic product. UNESCO collects the figures and the World Bank publishes them.
metadata.category: Government spending on health and education

metadata.summary: Public spending on health by general government, measured as a share of gross domestic product. Figures come from the World Health Organization and are published in the World Bank indicators.
metadata.category: Government spending on health and education

metadata.summary: Intentional killings recorded by police, counted per 100,000 people. The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime compiles national justice statistics, and the World Bank publishes the series.
Share of infants who die before their first birthday. The United Nations World Population Prospects estimates it from vital registration and surveys, and Our World in Data republishes the rate.
Annual percentage change in consumer prices, showing how fast the cost of a typical household basket rises. National statistical offices report the index, and the World Bank republishes it.
Share of people who used the internet during the past three months. National surveys and operator data are gathered by the International Telecommunication Union and published by the World Bank.

Average years a newborn would live if current death rates stayed unchanged. The United Nations population estimates calculate it from registered deaths and censuses, and Our World in Data republishes the series.

metadata.description: Life satisfaction, Cantril ladder, Gallup World Poll
metadata.summary: How people rate their life today, on a ladder from 0 to 10. Gallup asks this in its World Poll, and Our World in Data republishes the national average score.
Average years of formal schooling completed by adults aged 25 and older. UNESCO compiles school enrolment and attainment records, and Our World in Data republishes the national averages.

Active mobile-phone subscriptions, including prepaid accounts, counted per 100 people. A person may hold several lines. Operators report them to the International Telecommunication Union, and the World Bank publishes the series.

metadata.description: Employees usually working 50 or more hours per week, percentage of total employment
metadata.summary: Employees who usually work 50 hours or more a week on their main job, as a percentage of everyone in employment that year. The OECD labour-force statistics supply both counts.
Average mathematics score of 15-year-old students on the OECD PISA test. Schools are sampled to represent each country, and the comparable trend figures come from the PISA 2025 results annex.
Average reading score of 15-year-old students on the OECD PISA test. Schools are sampled to represent each country, and the comparable trend figures come from the PISA 2025 results annex.
Average science score of 15-year-old students on the OECD PISA test. Schools are sampled to represent each country, and the comparable trend figures come from the PISA 2025 results annex.

metadata.description: Outdoor air pollution exposure, population-weighted PM2.5
metadata.summary: Average outdoor exposure to fine particulate matter, weighted by where people live. Satellite and ground measurements are modelled by Washington University and compiled by Our World in Data.

Average number of days per year, over the five most recent full years, with at least one millimetre of rain. Counts use daily rainfall from the Open-Meteo historical archive, which republishes ECMWF ERA5 under the CC BY 4.0 license.

metadata.description: Real house price index, latest quarter
metadata.summary: Inflation-adjusted index of residential property prices, set to 100 in 2010. National sources report quarterly prices to the Bank for International Settlements, and the latest quarter of each year is kept.

Average number of days per year, over the five most recent full years, with at least half a centimetre of snow. Counts use daily snowfall from the Open-Meteo historical archive, which republishes ECMWF ERA5 under the CC BY 4.0 license.

Average number of days per year, over the five most recent full years, when the sun shines for at least seven hours. Counts use daily sunshine duration from the Open-Meteo historical archive, which republishes ECMWF ERA5 under the CC BY 4.0 license.

metadata.description: Average tax wedge, single person at the average wage
metadata.summary: Income tax plus employee and employer social contributions for a childless single person earning the average wage, as a share of labour costs. The OECD calculates this in Taxing Wages.
